heading: Repeal and savings
text: Section 358. (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding the repeal, it shall not affect the previous operation of the repealed Code; any right, obligation or liability acquired or incurred; any penalty or punishment incurred for offences committed against that Code; or any investigation, proceeding or remedy concerning such penalty or punishment. Such proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued or enforced, and such penalty imposed, as if the Code had not been repealed.
source: India Code / Official Gazette of India, Act 45 of 2023

heading: Recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means
text: Section 105. The process of conducting a search of a place or taking possession of property, including preparation of the seizure list and signing of the list by witnesses, shall be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably a mobile phone, and the police officer shall without delay forward the recording to the specified Magistrate.
source: India Code / Official Gazette of India, Act 46 of 2023

heading: Information in cognizable cases
text: Section 173(1). Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station. Electronic communication shall be taken on record on being signed within three days by the person giving it. Section 173(2) requires a free copy of the recorded information to be given forthwith to the informant or victim.
source: India Code / Official Gazette of India, Act 46 of 2023

heading: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
text: Section 187(2). A Magistrate may authorise detention in police custody for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole, or in parts, at any time during the initial forty days or sixty days out of the detention period of sixty days or ninety days, as the case may be. Section 187(3) separately limits total detention to ninety days for the specified serious-offence category and sixty days for other offences, subject to the statutory default-bail condition.
source: India Code / Official Gazette of India, Act 46 of 2023

heading: Repeal and savings
text: Section 531(1) repeals the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Under section 531(2)(a), if immediately before BNSS commencement any appeal, application, trial, inquiry or investigation was pending, it shall be disposed of, continued, held or made under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 as in force immediately before commencement, as if BNSS had not come into force.
source: India Code / Official Gazette of India, Act 46 of 2023

heading: Electronic or digital record
text: Section 61. Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic or digital record in evidence on the ground that it is an electronic or digital record, and such record shall, subject to section 63, have the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as any other document.
source: Ministry of Home Affairs / Official Gazette of India, Act 47 of 2023

heading: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record
text: Section 62. The contents of electronic records may be proved in accordance with section 63.
source: Ministry of Home Affairs / Official Gazette of India, Act 47 of 2023

heading: Admissibility of electronic records
text: Section 63 treats qualifying computer output as a document and makes it admissible without production of the original when the statutory conditions are satisfied. Those conditions address regular use, regular feeding of information, proper operation, and faithful reproduction or derivation. Section 63(4) requires the prescribed certificate identifying the electronic record and manner of production, giving device particulars, addressing the statutory conditions, and signed by the specified responsible person and expert; the Schedule includes hash details.
source: Ministry of Home Affairs / Official Gazette of India, Act 47 of 2023

heading: Repeal and savings
text: Section 170(1) repeals the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Under section 170(2), if immediately before BSA commencement any application, trial, inquiry, investigation, proceeding or appeal was pending, that matter shall be dealt with under the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 as in force immediately before commencement, as if BSA had not come into force.
source: Ministry of Home Affairs / Official Gazette of India, Act 47 of 2023
